estate_label: Higher education, research, and commercialization estate
domain: universities, laboratories, federal research awards, trustees, technology transfer, spinouts, licenses, and sponsored research
scope: Universities, affiliated laboratories, research centers, principal investigators, federal grants, sponsored research, technology-transfer offices, patents and assignments, licenses, spinouts, trustees, and corporate research partnerships. The estate separates research funding, invention, assignment, license, incorporation, investment, and procurement.
why_new_estate: Defense, AI, regulatory, nonprofit, and industrial-policy trails frequently originate in publicly funded research, yet the project lacks a corpus for the legal transition from research to company.

denominator_contract.unit: one research award or invention family linked through exact award, investigator, patent, assignment, license, and company identifiers
denominator_contract.inclusion_rule: Federal award records, official institutional pages, patent and assignment records, public license announcements, company filings, and later awards.
denominator_contract.exclusion_rule: Publication coauthorship as ownership; university affiliation as assignment; patent citation as technology transfer.
denominator_contract.time_window: historical through 2026-07-23, with each source query recording its own bounded window
required_null_controls: funded project with no located patent or spinout
spinout with no located federal award

source_routes.bounded_output: Federal research projects, application and core project numbers, investigators, organizations, funding, opportunity numbers, dates, and linked publications.
source_routes.residual_fog: Award data does not itself establish invention, assignment, license, spinout, or later contract; organization and investigator identities require joining.

source_routes.bounded_output: NSF awards since 1989 with award numbers, investigators, recipient organizations, programs, abstracts, dates, and amounts.
source_routes.residual_fog: Proposals are confidential; award records do not establish patents, licenses, commercialization, or ongoing employment.

source_routes.bounded_output: Award and transaction identifiers with separate ceiling, obligation, and outlay fields.
source_routes.residual_fog: Recipient identity, award hierarchy, subaward coverage, and performance reconciliation remain estate-specific.

source_routes.bounded_output: Contract opportunities, award notices, solicitation identifiers, and contracting data.
source_routes.residual_fog: Some APIs require a key; attachments, amendments, interested vendors, and source-selection files may require additional acquisition.

source_routes.bounded_output: Patent applications, patents, inventors, applicants, prosecution history, status, documents, and bulk/open-data identifiers.
source_routes.residual_fog: Applicant, assignee, inventor, beneficial owner, licensee, and implementing company are distinct; unpublished applications remain unavailable.

source_routes.bounded_output: Recorded patent and trademark assignment documents with assignor, assignee, reel/frame or conveyance identifiers, and execution dates.
source_routes.residual_fog: Recording is voluntary and does not validate the underlying transaction; unrecorded licenses and beneficial ownership remain.

source_routes.bounded_output: Institution-specific technology-transfer, license, spinout, conflict, annual-report, and commercialization disclosures.
source_routes.residual_fog: No complete official cross-institution denominator exists; license terms are often confidential and announcements require patent/company resolution.

decisive_output: award-to-commercialization chain with exact grant, investigator, institution, patent, assignment, license, company, funding, and contract identifiers
next_acquisition: join federal research awards to investigators, institutions, inventions, assignments, licenses, spinouts, and later public contracts
boundaries: A grant, publication, patent, license, spinout, investment, and government contract are different events. Sequence or institutional affiliation does not establish transfer or control.
A surveyed and prepared estate is not an acquired, completed, or finding-bearing estate.
Official source availability is not evidence of a subject overlap.
